questions.q: What is the real difference between pay-as-you-go and reserved instances?
options: Pay-as-you-go bills by actual usage with no commitment; reserved instances commit to 1-3 years for a significant discount
They are two names for the exact same billing model
Reserved instances are always billed by the hour with no discount
Pay-as-you-go requires a 3-year upfront commitment
questions.explain: Reserved instances trade a 1-3 year commitment for a discount, often 40-60% off, on steady workloads.

questions.q: What does the Azure Pricing Calculator let you do?
options: Estimate the monthly cost of a resource before you actually deploy it
Automatically cancel resources that exceed a budget
Change the region a resource is deployed in after the fact
Grant RBAC role assignments to a resource
questions.explain: It builds a cost estimate based on the service, region, and usage pattern you specify, before anything is created.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's own Cost Management documentation, what are its three key principles?
options: Visibility, accountability, and optimization
Speed, security, and scalability
Automation, replication, and encryption
Compute, storage, and networking
questions.explain: Visibility (see what you spend), accountability (know who owns it), and optimization (act on what you see) map directly onto the tool's features.

questions.q: What is a budget alert in Azure Cost Management?
options: A notification that fires when spending crosses a percentage of a set spending threshold
An automatic hard stop that deletes resources once a budget is reached
A monthly invoice email with no threshold logic
A tool for estimating cost before deployment
questions.explain: An alert fires at thresholds like 50%, 90%, or 100% of a budget, giving time to act before an invoice arrives.

questions.q: Which workload is the best fit for a reserved instance rather than pay-as-you-go?
options: A production database server running 24/7 for the next two years
A dev/test VM that's shut off most nights
A one-time proof-of-concept that runs for two days
A resource whose usage pattern is completely unpredictable
questions.explain: Reservations pay off on steady, predictable, long-running workloads — the opposite of a dev/test VM that's mostly off.
